newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasolines ease amid rain, lack of Tosco buys.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasolines ease amid rain, lack of Tosco buys.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline eased Monday, dealers said, as rain in California dampened weekend driving demand and Tosco held off buying in bulk after losing a key refinery unit last week.
"The market right now is generally weak," a California-based products broker said.
On Monday, CARB-grade gasoline in Los Angeles fell one cent from Friday to 79/80 cents a gallon, while Bay area gas stayed 78/79 cents.

Spot prices for wholesale gasoline rose as much 2.75 cents a gallon last week after a fire shut Tosco's 32,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker, a unit which upgrades fuel oils into light-end products, like diesel fuel and gasoline.
Conventional gasoline in L.A. dropped one cent to 76/77 cents, was steady around 71/72 cents.
"To get action after that, you need Tosco to be a vigorous buyer and they're not," a broker said.
Traders bought cargoes of CARB gasoline at 79.50 cents a gallon in L.A., they said. They bought conventional grade gasoline in the San Francisco for 75.75 cents.
Tosco, meanwhile, was reported to raise its terminal prices to discourage buying at a time when they could face shortages, traders said.
Brokers speculated the Tosco may have lost 20,000 bpd of gasoline production as a result of the fire.
"They'll have to buy, it's just a matter of when," a dealer said.
